blocks.en:
Behavior-Level Evolution: Distilling Reusable Skills from Branchus’s Trajectories. At the behavior level, Φ skill \Phi_{\mathrm{skill}} turns Branchus ’s reasoning trajectories into reusable skills.
These skills guide the agent at inference time and improve how it works while leaving its weights fixed.
Formally, Φ skill \Phi_{\mathrm{skill}} maps the trajectory pool to a set of new skills, Φ skill ​ ( 𝒮 ( t ) , 𝒯 ( t ) ) = 𝒮 ( t ) ∪ Δ ​ 𝒮 ( t ) \Phi_{\mathrm{skill}}(\mathcal{S}^{(t)},\mathcal{T}^{(t)})=\mathcal{S}^{(t)}\cup\Delta\mathcal{S}^{(t)} , through the composition Δ ​ 𝒮 ( t ) = ( Organize ∘ Filter ∘ Extract ∘ Eval ) ​ ( 𝒯 ( t ) ) \Delta\mathcal{S}^{(t)}=(\textsc{Organize}\circ\textsc{Filter}\circ\textsc{Extract}\circ\textsc{Eval})(\mathcal{T}^{(t)}) .
In the first stage, a judge model Eval scores the scheduler, searcher, and critic of the search team against role-specific rubrics.
The resolved outcome y q y_{q} is withheld from the judge, because forecast correctness is an imperfect proxy for reasoning quality.
In the second stage, Extract uses these scores to identify positive experiences from helpful but non-obvious actions, and negative experiences from recurring mistakes or failure modes.
Separating evaluation from extraction lets each step focus on a single judgment.
A Filter then discards weak experiences.
It removes those that merely restate a rubric, lack support in the trajectory, or only prescribe which evidence to use rather than how to forecast.
In the third stage, Organize grades each surviving experience into a four-level skill s = ( s 1 , s 2 , s 3 , s 4 ) s=(s_{1},s_{2},s_{3},s_{4}) : it keeps the concrete procedure applied in the trajectory verbatim as the most specific level s 4 s_{4} , and the three levels above it generalize that procedure step by step, first to the question type, then within its domain, and finally to a cross-domain principle s 1 s_{1} .
Each level stays within its role’s responsibility and remains independently applicable, so the skill can be matched at whichever level of abstraction fits a new question.
At inference time an agent retrieves skills by Equation ( 9 ), so a question without an exact precedent still benefits from a broader level.
Because distillation needs no gradient update, θ \theta stays fixed and only 𝒮 \mathcal{S} changes, in contrast to Φ rl \Phi_{\mathrm{rl}} .
This makes distillation cheap enough to repeat after every round.

blocks.en:
Environment-Level Evolution: Adversarial Skill Synthesis Targeting Branchus’s Weaknesses. At the environment level, Φ env \Phi_{\mathrm{env}} turns feedback from past forecasts into task-synthesis skills 𝒮 env \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{env}} .
These skills guide how Prometheus generates later questions, which reshapes the environment ℰ ( t + 1 ) \mathcal{E}^{(t+1)} and hence the next batch 𝒬 ( t + 1 ) \mathcal{Q}^{(t+1)} .
They specify what types of questions to construct and how to construct them, rather than how Branchus should answer them.
The goal is adversarial: expose categories of questions on which Branchus has struggled, while keeping every task clear, objectively verifiable, and reproducibly resolvable.
The update starts from the resolved triples { ( q , p ^ , y q ) } \{(q,\hat{p},y_{q})\} in 𝒯 ( t ) \mathcal{T}^{(t)} and their rewards.
We map each question to a category c = cat ​ ( q ) c=\textsc{cat}(q) by answer type and task feature, and aggregate the evaluable predictions into an error profile ρ ( t ) ( c ) = 𝔼 ( q , p ^ , y q ) : cat ​ ( q ) = c [ 1 − r ( q , p ^ ) ] , \rho^{(t)}(c)\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{(q,\hat{p},y_{q}):\,\textsc{cat}(q)=c}\big[\,1-r(q,\hat{p})\,\big], (12) the mean error rate for category c c .
We read this profile as evidence of category-level difficulty rather than as a direct diagnosis of a reasoning failure, since a single error may simply reflect the intrinsic uncertainty of an event.
The profiled categories include numerical forecasts, market prices, dynamic rankings, threshold judgments, and high-variance events.
The categories with the largest error, arg ⁡ max c ​ ρ ( t ) ​ ( c ) \arg\max_{c}\rho^{(t)}(c) , mark where Branchus is least reliable, and this signal directs where to construct new questions. Athena then turns the signal into reusable construction guidance 𝒮 env ( t ) = Synthesize ​ ( ρ ( t ) ) \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{env}}^{(t)}=\textsc{Synthesize}(\rho^{(t)}) .
Each synthesized skill specifies a target category, the conditions under which it applies, how to discover relevant events, rules for building questions, and quality constraints.
These skills enter the generator, so that Gen in ℰ ( t + 1 ) \mathcal{E}^{(t+1)} leans toward the identified weaknesses.
After the new questions are forecast and their outcomes become available, we update the error profile of Equation ( 12 ) and repeat the synthesis.
This loop lets Prometheus adapt the task distribution 𝒬 ( t ) \mathcal{Q}^{(t)} to Branchus ’s observed weaknesses across rounds, which keeps the recursion of Equation ( 4 ) from saturating.

blocks.en: 4.5 Models and Implementation
blocks.zh: 4.5 模式和实施

blocks.en:
Our evaluation pairs established agent harnesses with shared base LLMs as strong external baselines, and adds in-framework comparisons that isolate the core designs of DeepEvolve .
To make these comparisons fair, we enforce implementation parity.
Every harness runs on the same Prometheus questions, receives the same external tools under identical tool descriptions and a unified tool-calling format, and uses its own official prompt.
The only factors that vary across conditions are the harness design and the base LLM.
We avoid cross-paradigm comparisons that would break this parity, such as static-corpus question answering or dialogue, where evidence is already available rather than gathered under uncertainty from an unfolding world.
This keeps the gains reported in Section 2.2 attributable to the design of DeepEvolve rather than to mismatched task definitions.
We now give the three concrete settings behind this design.
blocks.zh:

每个被套都运行在相同的"普罗米修斯"(Prometheus)问题上,在相同的工具描述和统一工具调用格式下接收相同的外部工具,并使用自己的官方快取.
唯一因条件而异的因素是:被接地设计和底LLM.
我们避免进行可能打破这种等同的跨参数比较,例如静态公司问题回答或对话,因为那里已经存在证据,而不是在一个正在发展的世界的不确定性中收集。
这样,第2.2节中所报告的成果可归因于 " 深层演变 " 的设计,而不是任务定义不匹配。
我们现在给出这个设计背后的三个具体设置.

blocks.en:
Base LLMs and Agent Harnesses. We evaluate five representative frontier LLMs that span different model families and capabilities: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude-Opus-4.6, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and Qwen3.8-Max.
This range lets us test whether forecasting performance and evaluation robustness hold across model families rather than for a single base model.
We pair each base LLM with six agent harnesses: ReAct, MAS, OpenClaw, DeerFlow, MiroFlow, and Branchus , our purpose-built harness for real-world event forecasting.
These harnesses cover a broad range of designs: a lightweight reasoning-and-tool-use loop ( ReAct [ 27 ] ), a multi-agent system ( MAS ), and three deep-research pipelines ( OpenClaw [ 18 ] , DeerFlow , and MiroFlow ), spanning general-purpose reasoning frameworks and search-oriented systems.
This model × \times harness grid separates the contribution of the base LLM from that of the harness, and shows how harness design affects open-world forecasting across base models.
blocks.zh:
基地LLM和特工哈内斯 我们评价了五个具有代表性的前沿有限责任公司,它们跨越不同的模范家庭和能力:GPT-5.5、GPT-5.6-Sol、Claude-Opus-4.6、DeepSeek-V4-Pro和Qune3.8-Max。
这一范围使我们能够测试预测业绩和评价的稳健性是否贯穿于模范家庭,而不是单一的基础模型。
我们把每个基座LLM配为六个特工机组:ReAct,MAS,OpenClaw,鹿花,MiroFlow,和Branchus, 专为现实世界事件预测而建造的机组。
这些牵引装置涵盖广泛的设计:轻量级推理-工具-用环(ReAct [27]),多代理系统(MAS),和三条深研管(OpenClaw [18],鹿花和米罗花),跨越通用推理框架和面向搜索的系统.
这个模型×\times取用网格将碱基LLM的贡献与取用带的作用区分开来,并显示取用带设计如何影响跨取基模型的开放-世界预测.

blocks.en:
Prompt Specification. For each harness, we use its official prompt as released by the original authors, rather than writing our own.
This way, every framework runs in the configuration it was designed and tuned for, so performance differences reflect the harness design rather than our prompt engineering.
The complete prompt templates for the three modules of DeepEvolve are provided in Appendix D .
blocks.zh:
即时规格. 对于每一个绳索,我们使用它官方的即时 由原作者释放,而不是写我们自己的。
这样,每一个框架都运行在它所设计并调整的配置中, 所以性能的差异 反映的是带状设计,而不是我们的即时工程。
附录D提供了DeepEvolve三个模块的完整即时模板。

blocks.en:
External Tool Settings. We give the models a web search tool that issues queries and retrieves content, which grounds their forecasts in up-to-date evidence.
For Prometheus , we adopt the Codex [ 17 ] harness and use its built-in tools to crawl news from relevant web pages, which supplies the raw material for building questions.
We also design three local tools that expose the answer, the reasoning trajectory, and the collected evidence of the search team to the predict team of Branchus .
With these tools, the predict team reuses the search team’s outputs without issuing new external searches, so it reasons over exactly the evidence already collected.
blocks.zh:
外部工具设置 。 我们给模型一个网络搜索工具,发布查询和检索内容,以最新证据作为预测的依据。
对普罗米修斯来说,我们采用Codex [17] 利用并使用其内置工具从相关网页上爬取消息,这些网页为构建问题提供了原材料.
我们还设计出三个本地工具 揭示答案 推理轨迹 以及搜索组收集的证据
使用这些工具,预测团队会重新使用搜索团队的输出,而不发布新的外部搜索,因此它恰恰解释了已经收集的证据的原因.

Across the first three weeks Branchus attains the top overall rating; in the final week it remains among the strongest entrants, and we discuss the factors behind this week-to-week variation in Section 2 .

blocks.en: Appendix B Real World Event Forecasting
blocks.zh: 附录B 真实世界事件预测

blocks.en: B.1 2026 Nobel Prize
blocks.zh: B.1 2026 (中文(简体) ). 诺贝尔奖

blocks.en: To test our system on high-stakes, real-world events, we applied Branchus to forecasting the 2026 Nobel Prizes. This task carries genuine uncertainty, no training-set leakage, and a hard public resolution date. To make the evaluation fully pre-registered and verifiable, we published each forecast on X before the corresponding laureates were announced. Table 3 lists the five posts, one per prize. These timestamped, publicly committed predictions rule out hindsight and let any reader audit exactly what the system claimed, and when, against the subsequent announcements.
blocks.zh: 为了测试我们的系统 在高考,现实世界的事件, 我们应用了 Branchus 预测2026年诺贝尔奖。 这项任务具有真正的不确定性,没有训练有素的渗漏,以及一个难以公开解决的日期。 为了使评价能够充分预先登记和可核查,我们在宣布相应的获奖者之前就公布了X的每项预测。 表3列出了五个员额,每个奖项一个。 这些经过印章的公开承诺的预测排除了事后观察,让任何读者对系统所声称的以及随后的公告进行准确的审计。

blocks.en: Table 3: Pre-announcement forecasts for the 2026 Nobel Prizes, published on X before each laureate was announced.
blocks.zh: 表3:2026年诺贝尔奖公布前的预测,在每位获奖者宣布前在X上公布.

blocks.en: The 2026 Nobel Prizes are among the hardest forecasting targets imaginable. Each prize draws from a pool of thousands of plausible nominees, the committee’s deliberations are sealed for fifty years, and the final choice frequently rewards an outsider rather than the consensus front-runner. No historical pattern or odds board reliably anticipates the outcome, and the field of candidates any single forecaster can realistically track is a vanishing fraction of the true pool. A correct call therefore cannot be reverse-engineered from training data or market odds; it demands genuinely original evidence-gathering about who is in contention and why.
blocks.zh: 2026年的诺贝尔奖是难以想象的预测目标之一。 每个奖项都取自数千名可信的提名人,委员会的审议被封印了50年,最后的选择常常奖励外人而不是协商一致的先行者。 任何历史模式或概率板都无法可靠地预测结果,任何单一的预测者都能现实地追踪到的候选人领域是真正人才库中消失的一分点。 因此,不能从培训数据或市场差价中逆向提出正确的呼吁;它要求真正从原始证据中收集谁有争议和原因。

blocks.en: This difficulty defeats even the strongest systems. Fig. 12 compares the pre-announcement forecasts on the two prizes with the most extreme outsiders. The first is the Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded to Francis Halzen “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.” The second is the Nobel Peace Prize, awarded to Navi Pillay “for her efforts to promote peace and international law.” In both cases the eventual laureate was an outsider that essentially no forecaster took seriously: frontier agent systems, standalone web-search models backed by the most capable LLMs, and the Kalshi prediction market alike assigned the candidate no meaningful probability. None of them even listed the laureate, and none beat the trivial no-forecast baseline. Raw model strength, in other words, was not enough.
blocks.zh: 这种困难甚至打败了最强大的系统. 图12 将两个奖项的发布前预测与最极端的外人进行比较. 第一个奖项是诺贝尔物理学奖,颁发给弗朗西斯·哈尔岑(Francis Halzen),“因为他对冰管中微子天文台作出了决定性贡献并发现了天体物理源高能中微子 ” 。 第二个是诺贝尔和平奖,颁给纳维·皮莱“为促进和平和国际法而作的努力”。 在这两种情况下,最终的获奖者都是一个基本上没有预测者认真对待的局外人:前沿代理系统、由最有能力的LLMs支持的独立网络搜索模型,以及Kalshi预测市场都没有给候选人任何有意义的概率。 他们中没有任何人列出获奖者,也没有人超越微不足道的无预言基线。 换句话说,原始模型的力量是不够的。

blocks.en: Yet our system succeeded where they all failed. Branchus was the sole forecaster to surface and list either laureate, namely Halzen in Physics and Pillay in Peace, doing so in one of its three independent runs. Where every competitor left both laureates entirely off its slate, our system put them on the board. This ability to unearth a credible but overlooked candidate, rather than merely echoing consensus front-runners, reflects the broader and more exhaustive evidence that Branchus gathers before committing to a forecast.
blocks.zh: 然而,我们的系统在它们都失败的地方取得了成功。 Branchus是唯一一个可以浮出水面并列出获奖者名单的预报员,即物理学界的Halzen和和平界的Pillay。 每一个竞争者都把两位获奖者 都从名单中剔除 我们的系统把他们放到了董事会上 这种发掘一个可信但被忽视的候选人的能力,而不是仅仅重复协商一致的先行者的能力,反映了Branchus在承诺进行预测之前收集的更广泛和更详尽的证据。

blocks.zh: ((a))诺贝尔物理学奖:弗朗西斯·哈尔岑.

blocks.en: ((b)) Nobel Peace Prize: Navi Pillay.

blocks.en: Figure 12 : Pre-announcement forecasts for the 2026 Nobel Prizes in Physics and Peace. Each panel ranks forecasters by total Brier score (lower is better) against the no-forecast baseline of 1.0 1.0 . Both laureates were outsiders that no forecaster made a favourite, so no system beat the baseline. Branchus was the only forecaster to list either laureate, surfacing Halzen in Physics and Pillay in Peace in one of its three independent runs.
blocks.zh: 图12:2026年诺贝尔物理学与和平奖公布前预测. 每个小组根据布里尔总得分排名预测者(低于比1.0. 两位获奖者都是外人,没有预测者成为最受欢迎的,所以没有一个系统比基准要高. Branchus是唯一一个列出获奖者名单的预报员,他在其三项独立赛事中,将Halzen 和Pillay 放在物理领域。

blocks.en: Beyond the two outsider prizes above, the Literature and Economics prizes test forecasting on more consensus-driven fields where many forecasters cluster on the same front-runners. Fig. 13 shows, for each prize, the per-candidate probability every forecaster assigned before the announcement. The two prizes probe complementary behaviours. (1) Literature. Here our advantage is one of reliability. Although several forecasters placed mass on the eventual laureate, Anne Carson, only Branchus , OpenClaw, and GPT-6 Pro ranked her first in any run, and Branchus ’s other two runs both ranked her second. Every single one of our runs therefore placed the eventual laureate in the top two, a level of stability no competitor matched. Taken together with Peace, where Branchus alone surfaced the laureate, our system ranks the true winner in its top two across both prizes, a consistency that distinguishes a system that genuinely reasons about the field from one that happens to guess right once. (2) Economics. The 2026 prize was shared, but no forecaster, ours included, listed both laureates; every run surfaced only one of the two winners. On the finer-grained probability assigned to the laureate it did list, Branchus lands in the middle of the field, neither notably strong nor weak relative to the other systems, consistent with a shared prize whose second recipient none of the forecasters anticipated.
blocks.zh: 除了上面的两个外人奖之外,"文学与经济学奖"还测试了更多由共识驱动的领域的预测,许多预测者聚集在同一前锋. 图13显示每个奖项在公告前分配的每个预测器的每个扫描概率。 这两个奖项探索了互补行为. (1)文学. 在这里,我们的优势是可靠性。 虽然有几位预报员向最终的得奖者安·卡森(Anne Carson)投放质量,但只有Branchus,OpenClaw和GPT-6 Pro在任何跑道中排名她第一,而Branchus的其他两跑道都排名她第二. 因此,我们的每一次比赛都把最终的得奖者放在前二名,稳定程度与竞争对手不相上下。 与和平(Branchus one showed the Enversion)一起,我们的系统将真正的赢家排在两个奖项的前两名,这种一致性将真正说明球场理由的系统与偶然猜对一次的系统区分开来。 (2) 经济学。 2026年的奖金被分享,但是没有预测者,包括我们的奖项,列出两位得奖者;每次跑步都只浮出两个得奖者之一. Branchus在它所列举的给获奖者分配的更精细的概率上,在田地中间落地,与其他系统相比既不明显强又弱,这符合一个共同的奖项,其第二个受奖者没有预期到任何预测者。

blocks.en: This appendix specifies, in full, the metrics used to score the Prometheus -synthesized evaluation. Our goal is to characterize a forecaster along three complementary axes—how often it is right, how trustworthy its stated probabilities are, and how much compute it spends—rather than to collapse everything onto a single number. We write ℐ \mathcal{I} for the set of scored harness–LLM systems, index its members by i i , and set M = | ℐ | M=|\mathcal{I}| . Questions come in two families, which we handle separately: a choice track and a numeric track, denoted by the superscript t ∈ { c , n } t\in\{c,n\} . The question set of a track is 𝒬 t \mathcal{Q}^{t} and its cardinality is N t = | 𝒬 t | N^{t}=|\mathcal{Q}^{t}| .

Each axis is cut into three tiers at its empirical 1 / 3 1/3 and 2 / 3 2/3 quantiles within the track, with boundary values assigned to the lower tier.

blocks.en: Absolute and question-adjusted losses. Inside a stratum we report both an absolute level of error—mean Brier for choice questions, median 100 ​ WIS i ​ q / | y q | 100\,\mathrm{WIS}_{iq}/|y_{q}| for numeric questions—and a question-adjusted version that removes the effect of which questions each system happened to answer. For choice questions we subtract the per-question mean Brier, Δ ​ BS i ​ q = BS i ​ q − 1 M ​ ∑ j ∈ ℐ BS j ​ q , \Delta\mathrm{BS}_{iq}=\mathrm{BS}_{iq}-\frac{1}{M}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\mathrm{BS}_{jq}, and for numeric questions we use the log ratio of WIS to the question’s geometric-mean WIS, d i ​ q = ln ⁡ WIS ~ i ​ q − 1 M ​ ∑ j ∈ ℐ ln ⁡ WIS ~ j ​ q . d_{iq}=\ln\widetilde{\mathrm{WIS}}_{iq}-\frac{1}{M}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\ln\widetilde{\mathrm{WIS}}_{jq}. For the logarithm we replace a zero WIS by half the smallest positive WIS on the same question, or set the adjusted value to zero if every WIS there is zero; the pairwise win comparisons above still use the untouched WIS values. A negative adjusted loss means the system beats the question-level reference. These adjusted scores are averaged over the questions in each stratum, harness-level summaries take the arithmetic mean across base models, and normalized Brier differences divide each per-question score by 1 − 1 / K q 1-1/K_{q} , the Brier score of the uniform forecast.

blocks.en: Appendix D Prompt Templates
blocks.zh: 附录D 提示模板

blocks.en:
For completeness and reproducibility, this section collects the core prompt templates that drive the three modules of DeepEvolve .
We present them in the order in which they participate in one round of the recursive self-improvement loop (Algorithm 1 ): first the prompt with which Prometheus synthesizes forecasting questions (Appendix D.1 ); then the prompt with which Branchus gathers evidence and issues a probabilistic prediction (Appendix D.2 ); then the two prompts through which Athena learns from the resulting trajectories, namely the judge prompt that evaluates each trajectory (Appendix D.3 ) and the prompt that distils reusable skills from it (Appendix D.4 ); and finally the prompt with which Athena synthesizes adversarial task-construction skills that drive environment-level evolution (Appendix D.5 ).
Placeholders of the form {{…}} are filled in at runtime with the relevant question, trajectory, evidence, or skill content.
The templates below are lightly edited for presentation; the full runtime versions include additional formatting instructions and output schemas that we omit here for brevity.
blocks.zh:
为了完整性和可复制性,本节收集了驱动 DeepEvolve 三个模块的核心即时模板.
我们按他们参与一回合递归自改进循环(Agorithm 1)的顺序介绍这些结果:首先是普罗米修斯合成预测问题的即时性(附录D.1);然后是Branchus收集证据并发布概率预测的即时性(附录D.2);然后是雅典娜从由此产生的轨迹中学习的两个即时性能,即评价每个轨迹的法官即时性能(附录D.3)和从中分解可再利用技能的即时性能(附录D.4);最后是雅典娜合成驱动环境层面演化的对抗性任务构建技能的即时性能(附录D.5).
表格的占位符在运行时填入相关的问题、轨迹、证据或技能内容。
以下模板经轻度编辑后进行演示;全程版本包括额外的格式化指令和输出方案,我们在此省略,以简洁.

The prompt directs the model to read and operate the prediction-question-factory skill; Prompt D.1 reproduces that skill’s specification (its skill document SKILL.md ), which defines the construction CLI, build semantics, and the boundary of what may be published. When Athena has produced task-synthesis skills 𝒮 env \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{env}} (Appendix D.5 ), they are additionally injected into the {{synthesis_skills}} field to steer generation toward Branchus ’s weaknesses. We abridge the question-synthesis prompt for presentation, keeping the operative instructions and dropping the full output schema and reporting checklist.

blocks.en: Prometheus — Question Synthesis Use the $prediction-question-factory in the repository to actually construct a batch of objective, short-horizon, content-rich prediction questions (reading its SKILL.md and references/ in full), rather than merely providing a plan. Build parameters: horizon_hours = 24; target_count = 50 (a soft target — do not trade quality for quantity); use the default question bank without rewriting history. Execution. 1. Use the existing Bash/Python and web search/fetch tools. If a tool or runtime is unavailable, report the blocker; do not fake discovery, modify source or configuration, or silently fall back to the built-in adapters. 2. Run one bounded open-discovery round: actually attempt every site in the source list and follow valuable detail pages (not just snippets); do not pre-filter by expected yield or stop early on reaching the target. Truthfully distinguish produced drafts, read-but-unsuitable, access failure, and not attempted. 3. Build from both scheduled events and developing news; keep the most valuable primary question per event and any substantively different outcomes, without padding by repeated predicates or low-information rephrasings. 4. Every question must: be unknown at the batch forecast_cutoff ; have a clear objective choice/number answer space; use a stable event_key + predicate_key ; distinguish forecast_deadline , observation cutoff, and resolve_by ; respect the horizon; and use Beijing Time in question text, UTC in machine fields. 5. Validate the draft JSON, then run the formal build-open exactly once (sharing one build-and-publication pipeline with the bundled adapters); do not probe with build first or rebuild to make up a shortfall. 6. If the count is low or zero, report it truthfully rather than lowering objectivity, unknownness, or quality. Do not modify the Skill, adapters, configuration, or already-published questions. On completion, return a brief, batch-only report (bank path; run_id / batch_id / status ; cutoff/horizon; published count, shortfall, target-met; bundled vs. open-discovery counts; domain/source/answer-type/predicate distributions and distinct-event count; per-site attempt status; representative question_id s; notable limitations), basing all error causes only on actual records. This time, only construct questions — do not predict, resolve, score, export, or perform post-publication maintenance.
blocks.zh: 普罗米修斯-问题综述. 使用寄存器中的$prespect- question-factory来实际构建一批客观,短视,内容丰富的预测问题(读取其SKILL.md和参考文献/全文),而不只是提供计划. 构建参数:地平线_小时=24;目标_计数=50(一个软目标-不以质量换取数量);使用默认问题库而不重写历史. 处决 1. 使用现有的Bash/Python和网页搜索/查询工具。 如果一个工具或运行时间不可用,请报告阻断器;不要弄虚作假地发现,修改源或配置,或者默地倒回内置适配器. 2. 运行一圈有界限的开放-发现回合:实际尝试源列表中的每个站点,并遵循有价值的细节页(不仅仅是片段);不要通过预期的收成来预过滤或提前到达目标而停止. 真实地区分出产生的草稿,读取但不适合,访问失败,没有尝试. 3. 利用排定的活动和正在发展的新闻;保留每起事件和任何实质性不同的结果中最有价值的首要问题,而不通过重复的上游或低信息重写来补充。 4.每个问题必须:在批量预报中未知;有明确的客观选择/数字答案空间;使用稳定的事件_键+上游_键;区分预测-死线,观察截取和解决-by;尊重地平线;在问题文字中使用北京时间,UTC在机场. 5. 验证JSON草案,然后完全运行一次正式的建设开放(与捆绑的适配器共用一个建设和出版管道);不要先用建设或重建来弥补短缺。 6. 如果计数低或为零,应如实报告,而不是降低客观性、未知性或质量。 不要修改技能、适配器、配置或已经公布的问题。 完成后,返回一个简短的,只批量的报告(银行路径;run_id / spot_id / status;截取/范围;已公布的计数,短缺,目标满足;捆绑 vs开放-发现计数;域名/出自/回答-类型/预发和特异事件计数;每个站点尝试状态;代表性问题_id s;显著限制),将所有出错原因仅基于实际记录. 这一次,只构建问题——不预测,不解决,不计分,不输出,也不进行出版后维护.

blocks.en: Prometheus — Question-Factory Skill ( SKILL.md ) prediction-question-factory . Build batches of objective short-horizon prediction questions, or inspect and summarize their construction runs. For question construction only — not forecasting, answer lookup, resolution, settlement, scoring, export, or post-publication editing. Construction CLI. • python -m prediction_question_factory build [--horizon-hours H] [--target-count C] • python -m prediction_question_factory build-open [--horizon-hours H] [--target-count C] < questions.json • python -m prediction_question_factory inspect REF • python -m prediction_question_factory report RUN_ID An installed package provides the shorter pqf command for the same CLI; Python APIs are imported from prediction_question_factory . A normal build has only two semantic inputs, horizon_hours and the soft target_count : use user-requested values, else command defaults. Do not create per-site route, coverage, evidence, review, or selection request files. Build. Choose exactly one construction command per request: build for bundled adapters alone, or build-open when supplying agent-discovered drafts; never run build first as a probe. The chosen command owns source-isolated bounded concurrency and retries, semantic deduplication, draft validation, diversity-aware ranking, one system-owned forecast cutoff, and atomic publication. Quantity is a soft target: a completed run with a shortfall or zero publications is valid, and one failed source reduces recall only. Bundled adapters supply official calendars, feeds, and structured pages; report actual domain coverage, not the bundled profile’s potential coverage. For explicit open discovery, attempt every listed website using the news-discovery reference, without filtering by domain or stopping at target_count ; scheduled events and developing news may both yield objective choice or number drafts. Pipe a JSON array of constructed questions to build-open , which combines them with bundled adapters in the same publication pipeline; source_id identifies the discovery provider (default open-discovery ), and source URLs and resolution rules are optional. Inspect and report. Use inspect only when canonical details or a run diagnosis are requested, and report to summarize persisted and code-derived run facts. An empty source returned no eligible opportunity — this is not a fetch error; never infer a more specific shortfall cause from opportunities that were not persisted. Construction boundary. Every published question must: remain unknown at the batch cutoff; have an explicit choice or number answer space; have resolve_by after the cutoff and within the requested horizon; and have a stable event_key + predicate_key identity independent of wording and run ID. Authorities, source URLs, observation windows, and resolution rules improve a question when known but are not publication requirements, and a later resolver may skip a question whose answer it cannot observe. Typed templates and the executing agent own the semantic judgment that a question is objective and still unknown; the Python core validates only answer shape, identity, and time boundaries, and does not infer meaning, guarantee settlement, or fetch the future answer. inspect and report are read-only. Never forecast, settle, score, export, correct, retract, or maintain a published question through this skill. Conditional guidance. Read references/question-writing.md when adding or auditing a question template; references/news-discovery.md for open discovery or news/event-supply diagnosis; references/adapter-development.md (and only that source’s semantic note) when implementing or repairing a source adapter; and references/rolling-extension.md only when explicitly implementing rolling scheduling.
blocks.zh: 普罗米修斯-问题-事实技能 (SKILL.md) 预测-问题-因素. 构建一批客观短视预测问题,或者检查并总结其建设运行情况. 仅用于问题构建——不进行预测,解答查询,解析,结算,打分,输出,或出版后编辑. 建设CLI. • 蟒 -- -- m预测 -- -- 问题 -- -- 构筑[ -- -- 视时]  H • 蟒蛇 - 额 预测 _ 问题_ 构件构建- 打开 [-视距-小时] H] [-目标-计 C] < 问题.json • 蟒蛇-m 预测_问题_因素检查 REF • python - m 预测_问题_因素报告 RUN_ID 一个已安装的软件包为相同的 CLI 提供了更短的 pqf 命令; Python API 从预测_ question_factory. 导入. 一个普通的构建只有两个语义输入,即地平线_小时和软目标_计数:使用用户请求的值,否则命令默认. 不创建每个站点的路由,覆盖范围,证据,复核,或选择请求文件. 盖起. 每个请求精确选择一个构造命令:单独为捆绑的适配器构建,或者在提供代理发现的草稿时构建-打开;从不作为探测器先运行构建. 所选择的指挥部拥有源同位化的受限同位素和再生,语义分解,验证草案,多样性意识分级,一个系统自主的预测截断,以及原子出版. 数量是一个软目标:完成的运行,但出版物不足或为零是有效的,一个失败的来源只减少召回. Bundled适配器提供正式的日历、资料和结构化的页面;报告实际的域覆盖,而不是捆绑的简介的潜在覆盖。 为了明确公开的发现,尝试每个上市网站使用新闻发现参考,而不通过域名过滤或停止目标_计数;预定事件和正在发展的新闻可能同时产生客观选择或数字草稿. 管道一个 JSON 阵列构建- 打开, 将它们与捆绑的适配器合并在同一发布管道中; source_id 识别出发现提供者(默认开放- 发现), 源 URL 和 解析规则是可选的 。 审取并报. 只有在要求提出犬科细节或运行诊断时才进行检查,并提出报告,总结持续存在的和密码生成的事实。 空来源返回没有符合条件的机会——这不是取回错误;从未推断出没有持续的机会会造成更具体的短缺。 建筑界. 每一个已公布的问题必须:在批量断接时仍然未知;有明确的选择或数字解答空间;在断接后并在所请求的地平线内有解析;以及有一个独立于措辞和运行ID的稳定事件_key + 上游-key身份. 当局、源域URL、观察窗口和解析规则在已知但不是出版要求时改进了问题,后来的解析者可能跳过无法观察其答案的问题。 被打入的模板和执行代理拥有一个语义判断,即一个问题是客观的,仍然未知;Python核心只验证答案形状,身份,和时间界限,不推断意义,保证和解,或获取未来的答案. 检查和报告只读。 从不通过这种技能预测、结算、计分、导出、正确、收回或维持已公布的问题。 有条件地指导. 读取 在添加或审计问题模板时,参考/问题写作.md; 用于公开发现或新闻/事件提供诊断的参考/新闻-发现.md; 用于执行或修理源适配器时的参考/适应-发展.md(以及只有源的语义说明); 参考/滚动-扩展。 md 只在明确执行滚动调度时才使用。

blocks.en: Branchus factors forecasting into a search team and a predict team (Section 4.3 ). Prompt D.2 drives the search team’s evidence gathering and Prompt D.2 drives the predict team’s probabilistic judgement over the aggregated evidence. Both are conditioned on the retrieved skill subset Retrieve ​ ( q , a , 𝒮 ) \textsc{Retrieve}(q,a,\mathcal{S}) of Equation ( 9 ), injected into the {{skills}} field.

blocks.en: Branchus — Search Team (evidence gathering) Today is {{today}} . Your task is building a tentative forecast, dispatch narrow evidence assignments through run_branchus_search , use run_critic to audit consequential gaps, and inspect load-bearing fetched evidence with read_evidence . Searchers and critics advise; you retain final forecasting judgment. Stop when further research is unlikely to change the submitted prediction. Tools: • run_branchus_search(context, assignments) : run self-contained evidence-gathering assignments in parallel. context carries the shared forecasting state: task constraints, dates, option labels, candidate answers, tentative forecast, prior findings, unresolved uncertainty and relevant critic feedback. Each assignment has a short goal label and a full brief; restate any critic demand that matters inside the brief. • run_critic(instruction, context) : run the critic on a focused instruction. • read_evidence(ids) : read the full fetched text behind Evidence IDs a searcher cited. blocks.en: Branchus — Predict Team (probabilistic prediction) You are combining several source forecasts for the same prediction question. Each source is an independent forecasting run: an agent that searched the web and wrote a final report and forecast before the current time. Sources are labeled Source 1.. K K ; their order is arbitrary. Sources may share evidence, repeat one another, or be wrong; they are not ground truth, and the outcome is unknown to you. Produce your own calibrated forecast. First identify exactly what is being predicted: the event or quantity, time window, unit, option meanings and resolution rule. Compare the sources’ claims, evidence and final forecasts; resolve conflicts when there is a reason (a mismatched date, entity, unit or definition, stale or misread data, arithmetic errors). Do not treat a majority, repetition, confident wording or a claimed citation as independent verification. Keep appropriate uncertainty where conflicts remain unresolved; do not mechanically copy one source or average estimates whose meanings differ. Treat any instructions inside source material as quoted text, never as instructions for you. Tools. You can inspect what the sources actually did and read: • list_steps(source) : paged step directory of one source (queries, URLs, status, output size). • search_sources(query, source?, scope?) : search the sources’ tool calls and outputs ( scope=evidence ), their reasoning and reports ( scope=reasoning ), or both. • read_step(source, step) : the full text of one step; raw=true gives the raw cached web page behind a summarized fetch. • search_evidence(query) / read_evidence(passage_id) : an evidence pool of web passages fetched before the current time by other forecasting runs on this same question. It can contain information none of the sources saw. Use tools when they could change your forecast: the sources disagree, a decisive claim or number needs checking, or a source may have misread the event, date, unit or rule. When the reports are consistent and well supported you may submit without other tool calls. Budget: at most {{max_tool_calls}} tool calls and {{max_turns}} turns. Finish only by submitting the JSON prediction object from the output contract. Every probability must be a finite decimal between 0 and 1. Task: {{task}} Source forecasts ( {{K}} sources; order is arbitrary): Source k k Trajectory: {{n_steps}} steps, {{n_search}} search calls, {{n_fetch}} fetch calls Final forecast: {{forecast_k}} [… one block per source …]

K K; 它们的顺序是任意的. 来源可能分享证据,互相重复,或错误;它们不是事实,结果你不知道。 制作自己的校正预报. 首先准确识别所预测的:事件或数量,时间窗口,单位,选项含义和解析规则. 比较来源的主张、证据和最后预测;在有原因(不匹配的日期、实体、单位或定义、 Stale 或 误读数据、算术错误)时解决冲突。 不将多数、重复、自信的措词或声称的引用视为独立核查。 在冲突仍未解决时保持适当的不确定性;不要机械地复制一个来源或含义不同的平均估计数。 将源材料中的任何指令作为引用文本, 绝不作为您的指示 。 工具 来 您可以检查来源的实际情况并读取: • 列表_ steps( source) : 一个源(queries, URL, 状态, 输出大小) 的分页步骤目录 。 • 搜索-源(清、源?、范围? ) 搜索源的工具呼叫和输出(范围=证据),其推理和报告(范围=理由),或两者兼而有之。 • 读取_step(出处,出处):一个步骤的全文;生=真,在摘要取取取后给出了被取取取的原始缓存网页. • 搜索_证据(清)/读_证据(通过_id): 其他预测在目前之前收集到的关于同一问题的证据库。 它不能包含任何消息来源所看到的信息。 当工具可以更改您的预测时使用:来源不同意,决定性的主张或数字需要检查,或者来源可能错误地读取事件,日期,单位或规则. 当报告内容一致并得到充分支持时,您可不使用其他工具调用而提交报告。 预算:最多为QQmax_tool_calls}}工具调用和XQmax_turns}}. 仅通过提交输出合同中的 JSON 预测对象来完成 。 每个概率必须是0到1之间的有限小数. 任务: QQTask 源预测 (QQQ; 顺序是任意的): 出处: k k 轨迹: {{n_ steps}} 步骤; {{n_ search}} 搜索呼叫; {{n_fetch}} 获取呼叫 最后预测:[.每个来源一个区块.]

blocks.en: The first stage of behaviour-level evolution, Eval , scores Branchus ’s trajectory one action at a time: each step is attributed to the single role that produced it (one of scheduler, planner, searcher, reasoner, critic) and judged in isolation against that role’s rubric, with the resolved outcome y q y_{q} withheld so that the judgement reflects the process rather than the outcome (Section 4.4 ). The driver ( main.py ) dispatches each step to the matching template: Prompt D.3 is the worker-step judge, while the scheduler is instead judged over its full decision trace. Every step is scored independently by each judge model in the ensemble, and the per-dimension verdicts are aggregated by their median. The {{role}} , {{dimensions}} , and {{rubric}} fields are specialized per role. These per-action scores and observed_issues are the input to the extraction stage of Appendix D.4 .
blocks.zh: 行为层面进化的第一阶段,Eval,分数 Branchus的轨迹一次一个动作:每个步骤都归于产生这个动作的单一角色(排程者、计划者、搜索者、理性者、评论者),并且根据这个角色的分数进行孤立判断,结果确定后y q y q q q ) 扣下,以便判断反映过程而不是结果(第4.4节)。 驱动程序( 主. py) 发送到匹配模板的每个步骤 : 迅速D.3是工人级法官,而排队者则被判断为其完全的裁决跟踪。 每一步由综艺节目中每个评委模型独立得分,每分评委的评委根据他们的中位数汇总. 以及每个角色都具有专业性。 这些每个动作分数和所观察到的_问题都是附录D.4的取出阶段的输入.

blocks.en: Athena — Action-Level Evaluation (judge) You are an expert evaluator of forecasting reasoning processes . You judge one step performed by a single agent role, scored only against that role’s own responsibility. You are not told the true outcome , and you must not try to guess it: a correct forecast can rest on flawed reasoning, and sound reasoning can still miss an uncertain event. Judge the process , not the result. Role under evaluation: {{role}} (scheduler / planner / searcher / reasoner / critic) Task context: {{question}} , {{cutoff_date}} , {{answer_type}} , {{choices}} The step under evaluation. You are given two separate blocks and must not confuse them: • given_to_this_step — the description, subtask, and query handed to the step as background. Use it to judge relevance, but it is not this step’s own work; never attribute its content to this step. • produced_by_this_step — the step’s own answer, status, statistics, and structured action trace (for a searcher, also the links it read). Score only this. {{given_to_this_step}} / {{produced_by_this_step}} / {{prior_context}} Dimensions to score: {{dimensions}} with rubric {{rubric}} . Instructions. 1. For each rubric dimension, return an integer score in 1 1 – 5 5 and a rationale grounded in specific content of produced_by_this_step . 2. List any observed_issues ; each must carry an issue , a severity ( minor / major / critical ), the quoted evidence , the related_dimensions it affects, and a rubric_gap explaining which rubric expectation it violates. A major issue must be reflected in a low score ( ≤ 3 \leq 3 ) on a related dimension, a critical issue in a very low one ( ≤ 2 \leq 2 ). Return a strict JSON object with exactly the keys dimensions (one entry per rubric dimension) and observed_issues ; no additional top-level keys are allowed.

blocks.en: Given the per-action evaluation of Appendix D.3 , Extract distils the surviving experience — a non-obvious action that helped or a recurring trap — from the trajectory, Filter discards weak candidates, and Organize then grades each experience into one role-specific four-level skill s = ( s 1 , s 2 , s 3 , s 4 ) s=(s_{1},s_{2},s_{3},s_{4}) (Section 4.4 ). The concrete procedure actually applied in the trajectory is kept verbatim as the most concrete level, and the levels above it generalize that procedure step by step — first to the question type, then within the broader domain, and finally to a cross-domain principle — giving the schema ordered from abstract ( s 1 s_{1} ) to concrete ( s 4 s_{4} ). The case study of Appendix E.3 shows both artifacts: the raw extracted experience (Prompt E.3 ) and the graded four-level skill it becomes (Prompt E.3 ). Prompt D.4 shows the grading template; the {{role}} and {{role_contract}} fields bind the skill to one role’s responsibility and its allowed and forbidden actions, and the {{experience}} and {{evidence_packet}} fields carry the extracted experience together with the trajectory evidence that supports it.

(第4.4节)。 实际在轨迹中采用的具体程序作为最具体的级别,上面的级别逐个概括该程序——先是问题类型,然后是更广泛的领域,最后是跨领域原则——赋予从抽象(s 1 s_{1})到混凝土(s 4 s_{4})的指令计划. 附录E.3的案例研究显示了两种文物:原始取出的经验(Prompt E.3 )和分级的四级技能(Prompt E.3 . Pournal D.4 显示了分级模板; Q{{role}}和 {{role_contract}} 字段将技能绑定在一个角色的责任及其允许和禁止的行动上; Q{{经验}}和 {{证据_-packet}} 字段将所取出的经验与支持其的轨迹证据相接.

blocks.en: Athena — Skill Extraction You distil one reusable forecasting skill from an evaluated experience. A skill is a compact piece of procedural know-how about how to forecast , written at four levels of abstraction. Each level is a title , a situation in which it applies, an instruction to carry out, and keywords ; it describes how to forecast, never the specific answer to this question. Role: {{role}} with contract {{role_contract}} (responsibility, allowed / forbidden actions) Experience and supporting evidence: {{experience}} / {{evidence_packet}} Instructions. 1. Write the skill as a four-level hierarchy from concrete to abstract: • s 4 s_{4} : the concrete procedure exactly as applied in this trajectory, kept verbatim; • s 3 s_{3} : its generalization to this question type; • s 2 s_{2} : its generalization within the broader domain; • s 1 s_{1} : a general, cross-domain forecasting principle. Each level up must be strictly broader than the one below while preserving the same core mechanism and the conditions required for the instruction to hold. 2. Stay inside the role’s contract: the instruction must be an action this role is allowed to take, and must never attribute a forbidden action or an unperformed step. 3. Keep every level immediately executable and free of outcome leakage — do not encode the resolved answer, and do not merely restate a rubric. 4. If the experience cannot support a faithful four-level skill for this role, return status : unable with a brief reason instead of forcing one. Return one strict JSON object with the four levels (each with its title , situation , instruction , and keywords ) and the role the skill applies to.

blocks.en:
Athena — Adversarial Task-Synthesis Skill Generation You design task-construction guidance for a forecasting-question generator. Your goal is to challenge the forecaster by guiding future question generation toward categories in which it has performed poorly. Every question must be clearly defined, have an objectively verifiable outcome, and be resolvable through a reproducible process. Specify the question types to target and the procedures for constructing them, without prescribing how to forecast their outcomes. Derive reusable construction guidance from the supplied error profile. Observed error profile (per-category error rates and sample counts): {{error_profile}} Instructions. 1. Prioritize categories with high observed error rates in the supplied profile, taking sample size into account. Use these rates as prioritization signals for question construction
and selection. Interpret them as indicators of category-level difficulty for the forecaster, rather than conclusive evidence of systematic reasoning flaws, since individual errors may reflect inherent uncertainty in the events being forecast. 2. For each category supported by the evidence, define reusable rules that make questions more challenging in ways specific to the category while keeping them objective. Write guidance for constructing questions, never for predicting their answers. 3. Keep each question objective and reproducibly resolvable, with its outcome unknown at forecast_cutoff . Verify that each rule is supported by the supplied profile and check for consistency with the generator contract. Return a list of task-synthesis skills, each with fields: target_category , applicability , discovery_procedure , construction_rules , quality_constraints .

和选择。 将其解释为预测者在类别层面难度的指标,而不是系统性推理缺陷的确凿证据,因为个别错误可能反映所预测事件固有的不确定性. 2. 对于有证据支持的每个类别,界定可重复使用的规则,使问题更具有特定类别的挑战性,同时保持其客观性。 为构建问题写出指导,永远不要为预测答案写出指导. 3. 保持每个问题的目标并可以重新解决,其结果在预测_截止时不得而知。 核实每项规则是否得到所提供的剖面图的支持,并检查是否符合发电机合同。 返回任务合成技能列表,每个选项包含:目标-类别,适用性,发现-程序,构造-规则,质量-约束.

blocks.en: Appendix E Case Study
blocks.zh: 附录E 案例研究

blocks.en:
To make the recursive self-improvement loop concrete, this section walks through a single worked example in the order the three modules act within one round: we first show how Prometheus synthesizes a forecasting question, contrasting a draft produced before environment-level optimization with the sharper, weakness-targeted draft produced after a task-synthesis skill is applied (Appendix E.1 ); we then show how Branchus forecasts such a question, tracing the search and predict teams through to a probabilistic answer (Appendix E.2 ); and finally we show the reusable skill that Athena distils from that trajectory (Appendix E.3 ).
Together these snapshots illustrate how the products of one round — a sharper question, a trajectory, and a skill — become the raw materials of the next.
blocks.zh:
为了使递归自改进循环混凝土,本节通过一个单一的例子,按三个模块在一回合内行动的顺序排列:我们首先显示普罗米修斯如何合成一个预测问题,将环境层面优化前生成的草稿与应用任务合成技能后生成的更尖锐、针对弱点的草稿作对比(附录E.1);然后显示Brancus如何预测这样一个问题,追踪搜索和预测队伍,直至概率化的答案(附录E.2);最后,我们显示雅典娜从该轨迹中脱落的可再利用技能(附录E.3)。
这些快照合在一起说明了一回合的产品——更尖锐的问题、轨迹和技能——如何成为下一回合的原材料。

blocks.en: E.1 Prometheus: Skill-Conditioned Question Synthesis
blocks.zh: E.1 普罗米修斯:技能问题综合

blocks.en:
We first show how the same crawled source material yields different questions before and after environment-level optimization. The two drafts below are drawn from a controlled comparison in which we ran the question-synthesis pipeline over an identical corpus of calendars and feeds twice: once with the baseline generator and once after a task-synthesis skill from 𝒮 env \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{env}} (Appendix D.5 ) is injected into the {{synthesis_skills}} field of the Prometheus prompt (Prompt D.1 ).
The two batches resolve to the same underlying events, which lets us read the effect of the skill directly: for a given event, the baseline generator fans out over many predicates and tends to retain the easy, nearly-decided ones (“who wins”, a coarse category band), whereas the skill-steered generator is more selective and keeps the sharp, weakness-targeted predicate — typically a numerical forecast or a threshold judgment , two of the categories on which Branchus ’s error profile ρ ( t ) \rho^{(t)} (Equation ( 12 )) is highest.
Quantitatively, the skill-steered batch emits fewer questions per event ( 1.29 1.29 vs. 2.15 2.15 on the shared events) and concentrates them on these harder predicates, rather than padding the batch with low-information rephrasings.
Prompt E.1 shows a baseline draft produced without any task-synthesis guidance; Prompt E.1 shows the draft produced once the skill is applied, illustrating how environment-level evolution sharpens the question toward Branchus ’s weaknesses while preserving objectivity and reproducible resolvability.
All questions are synthesized in Chinese; we translate them here for presentation, preserving the original sources, reference series, and resolution rules.

我们首先展示了同样的被爬行的源材料如何在环境水平优化前后产生不同的问题. 以下两项草案取自一个控制比较,我们用一套相同的日历和输入符对提问-合成管道进行两次操作:一次与基线生成器,一次是在S env \ mathcal{S}_{\ mathrm{env}}(附录D.5)的任务-合成技能后注入了Prometheus poil的Q{{ synthes_skilly}} (Prompt D.1).
这两个批次决定了同样的基本事件,让我们直接阅读技能的影响:对于一个特定事件,基线生成器的爱好者超越许多上游,倾向于保留容易的、几乎决定的(“谁胜出,一个粗糙的类别”),而技能型生成器则更具选择性,并保持尖锐的、针对弱的上游——通常是数字预测或阈值判断,这是Branchus错误简介所对应的两个类别 ^ (t)\rho^{(t)} (等分(十二))为上.
从数量上看,技能型批次每起事件发出的问题较少(共享事件1.29 1.29 vs 2.15 2.15),并集中处理这些更难的上游,而不是用低信息重写来补充批次.
Express E.1 显示了一份没有任务综合指导的基线草案; Express E.1 显示了技能运用后产生的草案,说明了环境层面的演变如何将问题推向了Branchus的弱点,同时保持客观性和可复制的可解性。

blocks.en: Case Study — Prometheus Question (Before Optimization) Shared source material. The official start list and record table for the Women’s 77 kg weightlifting final (Group A) at the 20th Asian Games (Aichi–Nagoya), scheduled for 16:00 Beijing time on 2026-09-27. The start list gives the five entrants and their declared entry totals: LKHAGVAJAV Bolor-od (MGL) 170 kg, KARIMI Reihaneh (IRI) 240 kg, KIM Iseul (KOR) 240 kg, HE Renxiu (CHN) 255 kg, ZHUMAGALI Ayanat (KAZ) 245 kg; the record table lists the world record (278 kg), the Asian Standard (273 kg), and the Asian Games Standard (268 kg). Baseline draft (no task-synthesis skill). • Question: “Who wins the gold medal in the Women’s 77 kg event (highest total)?” • Category / answer format: contest-winner; single choice over the five entrants plus “no valid total / no gold awarded”. • Remark: The outcome is largely pre-determined by the public entry totals — HE Renxiu’s declared total (255 kg) leads the field by at least 10 kg — so the question collapses to a near-certain favourite and carries little forecasting signal. It exercises none of Branchus ’s weak categories.

blocks.en: Case Study — Prometheus Question (After Optimization) Shared source material. The same start list and record table for the Women’s 77 kg weightlifting final as in Prompt E.1 . Skill-steered draft (with a task-synthesis skill for the numerical-forecast category). • Applied skill: target category numerical forecasts / threshold judgments ; construction rule — reframe a contest around a precise numeric quantity measured against a cited reference level, keeping a single objective ground truth. • Question: “What is the gold medallist’s total (best snatch plus best clean-and-jerk), in kilograms?” (with the record table’s 268 kg Asian Games Standard supplied as a salient reference level). • Category / answer format: level; integer-valued number (kg). • Remark: Even granting the likely winner, the exact total remains genuinely uncertain — it depends on in-competition attempt selection and makes/misses — and the cited 268 kg standard turns it into a threshold the forecaster must reason about. The question is hard in precisely the numerical dimension ρ ( t ) \rho^{(t)} flags, yet remains objective and resolvable from a single official results page.

blocks.en: A second example, drawn from a different domain in the same comparison, shows the sharpening is not specific to sports. From the identical source — the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) daily AQI bulletin for Delhi, whose preceding seven days read 118,160,169,178,154 , 145 , 78 118,160,169,178,154,145,78 — the baseline generator asks for the coarse air-quality category (a three-way band of “0–100 / 101–200 / 201+”), which the recent trend already pins to “Moderate” with near-certainty; the skill-steered generator instead asks for the exact integer Index Value published in that day’s bulletin, a numerical forecast with a precise ground truth and a reliable public resolution source. In both examples the environment-level skill holds the source material, the objectivity, and the reproducible resolvability fixed, and moves only the difficulty of the question into the category where Branchus is weakest.

blocks.en: E.2 Branchus: A Worked Prediction
blocks.zh: E.2 联合国 分支:工作预测

blocks.en: We next trace Branchus on a question posed by Prometheus , such as the skill-steered weightlifting total of Prompt E.1 . The search team decomposes the question, gathers and critiques evidence, and hands a structured evidence summary to the predict team, which reconciles the evidence into a calibrated probability, recording the full trajectory τ = ( { τ s ( j ) } j , τ p ) \tau=(\{\tau_{\mathrm{s}}^{(j)}\}_{j},\tau_{\mathrm{p}}) . To make the two evolution channels of Athena concrete, we show Branchus forecasting the same question under three configurations: Prompt E.2 is the baseline, before any evolution; Prompt E.2 adds the distilled skill of Appendix E.3 to the retrieved skill set, illustrating behaviour-level evolution ( Φ skill \Phi_{\mathrm{skill}} ) without touching the weights; and Prompt E.2 uses the predict-team weights after RFT, illustrating parameter-level evolution ( Φ rl \Phi_{\mathrm{rl}} ). Holding the question fixed isolates the effect of each channel on the trajectory and the resulting prediction.
blocks.zh: 接下来我们追踪Branchus, 普罗米修斯提出的一个问题, 例如技能取重, 搜索组将问题分解,收集并批判证据,将结构化的证据摘要交给预测组,将证据调和为校正概率,记录出完整轨迹= ({τ s (j)} j, τ p)\tau= (\{\ tau_{\ mathrm{ s}}^{ (j)}\}_{j},\tau_{\ mathrm{p}}). 为了让雅典娜混凝土的两个进化道,我们向分公司展示在三个配置下预测同一个问题: Express E.2是基线,在任何演化之前; Express E.2将附录 E.3所蒸馏出的技能添加到被取回的技能集中,说明行为层次的演化(XQ技能\Phi_{\mathrm{skill}};和 Express E.2使用RFT之后的预测-团队权重,说明参数层次的演化(XQRl\Phi_{\mathrm{rl}})). 持有问题固定隔离了每个通道对轨迹的影响以及由此产生的预测.

blocks.en:
Case Study — Branchus Prediction Trajectory (Baseline, Before Evolution) Question. Mirum Pharmaceuticals’ oral ALK2 inhibitor zilurgisertib (licensed from Incyte) for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is under FDA Priority Review, with a PDUFA target date of Saturday, 2026-09-26. Its pivotal Phase 2 PROGRESS trial missed the primary endpoint (81% reduction in new heterotopic-ossification lesions, p = 0.0986 p=0.0986 ), but reduced new-lesion volume by > 99 % >\!99\% ( p < 0.0001 p<0.0001 ). As of 22:30 ET on Friday, 2026-09-25, which FDA outcome has been publicly announced ? Options: approved / crl / extended / none Forecast: made on 2026-09-24; output a probability over the four options. Resolution: first public company or FDA announcement before the cutoff. Search team trajectory ( τ s \tau_{\mathrm{s}} ). • Decomposition. The scheduler first separates what the question resolves on ( was something announced by the cutoff ) from what it seems to ask ( what FDA decides ). That gives three sub-questions:
(i) premise check: does the drug, the Incyte licence, the Priority Review, and the Saturday PDUFA date really exist as stated;
(ii) timing: given a weekend goal date, how likely is it that FDA acts by Friday, and that the sponsor makes it public before 22:30 ET;
(iii) the decision itself: approval vs. complete response letter (CRL) vs. review extension, weighing a missed primary endpoint against a very strong secondary endpoint and FOP-specific precedent.
It forms an initial forecast ( approved 0.47, crl 0.22, extended 0.03, none 0.28) and then runs three search rounds and one critic call. • Retrieval. Searchers covered: – primary filings: SEC EDGAR full-text search (45 filings mention zilurgisertib), Mirum’s Q1/Q2 2026 10-Q and 8-K filings, and Incyte’s Q2 release, which together confirm the April 2026 licence ($16M upfront, $25M milestone due on approval) and the PDUFA date; – regulator channels: the FDA newsroom and the 2026 Novel Drug Approvals list, both checked up to the last available date; – market and calendar trackers: pdufa.bio decision pages, Mirum’s investor-relations and Business Wire feeds; – trial data: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05090891 and a third-party PDUFA primer, which added the 48-week durability data; – price action: daily MIRM prices compared with the XBI biotech index; – a weekend-PDUFA precedent set: sponsor press-release and 8-K timestamps for 11 cases from 2019–2026 (Zurzuvae, BYSANTI, YUVIWEL, GENGLYCOS, KRESLADI, bitopertin, Joenja, RGX-121, AVT05, deramiocel, tab-cel). • Critique. The critic accepted the evidence base but challenged two calibration choices.
(1) none was being treated as a leftover bucket rather than a modelled outcome. Announcement delay is much more likely after a CRL than after an approval, so P( none ) should sit in the low-to-mid 0.30s, not 0.28.
(2) The earlier FOP drug Sohonos does not license ignoring a failed randomised primary endpoint, so the conditional approval probability should drop from about 0.62 to 0.52–0.58.
It also raised a recency gap: the decisive window (ET Sep 24–25 up to 22:30) had not been observed, so silence through Sep 23 cannot be read as evidence. It requested targeted checks of every public channel up to the cutoff, plus a timing base rate split by outcome. • Evidence summary. – Premise fully verified. As of the last data available (evening ET 2026-09-23), there was no approval, CRL, extension, advisory committee, or major amendment on record. – Mirum’s own 10-Q flags CRL risk. The CEO cited “launch readiness”. The stock fell 11% into the date, including an unexplained − 7 % -7\% day on Sep 18. – Key structural finding: whether an outcome is announced in time depends on what the outcome is. Approvals were public by the Friday before the weekend goal date in 4/4 cases, and FDA has never dated an approval on a weekend. CRLs were public by Friday in only 2/6 cases. The one comparable extension was announced on the following Monday. So none mostly contains CRLs or extensions that had not yet been announced. – Approval case: Sohonos was approved on the same lesion-volume measure from a single-arm study, and recent FDA rare-disease evidence principles support flexibility. CRL case: the pre-specified primary endpoint formally failed in a single trial with only 6 events. – Decision probabilities: approval ≈ 0.58 \approx 0.58 , CRL ≈ 0.35 \approx 0.35 , extension ≈ 0.04 \approx 0.04 . Combined with the outcome-specific announcement probabilities, the forecast is approved 0.52 / crl 0.16 / extended 0.02 / none 0.30. Predict team trajectory ( τ p \tau_{\mathrm{p}} ). • Reconciliation. The predict team receives four independent search trajectories τ 1 , … , τ 4 \tau^{1},\dots,\tau^{4} . It does not average their outputs. It treats them as four partly overlapping evidence sets and re-derives the forecast from the combined evidence. The question resolves on what has been announced by 22:30 ET Friday, so the team splits it into two parts and reconciles each one separately: (i) what FDA actually decides, and (ii) whether that decision is public before the cutoff. – Cross-validated facts. A fact is treated as settled only if at least two trajectories reached it through different sources: * Saturday PDUFA date: Mirum’s 8-K and 10-Q, plus independent PDUFA trackers. * Trial numbers: the missed primary endpoint (1/32 vs. 5/31 patients with new lesions, p = 0.0986 p=0.0986 , only 6 events) against a > 99 % >99\% cut in new-lesion volume. Taken from the company’s filings and from the trial registry or third-party summaries. * No advisory committee and no major amendment. * Nothing announced on any channel up to Sep 23–24: SEC filings, company press releases, the FDA newsroom, and the novel-approval list. One signal comes from a single trajectory only: an unexplained single-day 7% fall in the stock on Sep 18. It is kept, but weighted as weak. – Combining evidence on the decision. Two trajectories reported the Sohonos precedent in two different ways: * one found that FDA accepted “reduction in new heterotopic-ossification volume” as the basis for approving that drug; * another found that this approval rested on a single-arm study compared with natural history. A third trajectory’s critic warned that the precedent may not carry over unless the endpoint and multiplicity design are checked.
Put together, the precedent supports the lesion-volume endpoint (and zilurgisertib’s randomised, placebo-controlled volume result is stronger evidence). It does not settle the failed primary endpoint, which stays a real risk of a complete response letter (CRL). That risk is backed by the 2025–26 efficacy CRLs found in one trajectory.
On the other side, other trajectories added independent cases of rare-disease approval on secondary or surrogate endpoints (tofersen, eteplirsen), plus FDA’s current rare-disease evidence principles.
The trajectories’ own estimates of the approval share span roughly 0.53–0.60. Two of them cited the same third-party approval odds (64–70%). One critic pointed out that these odds refer to eventual approval, not to an approval announced by the cutoff, so the team uses them only as an upper check.
Net result: P ⁡ ( approve ∣ action ) ≈ 0.57 P(\text{approve}\mid\text{action})\approx 0.57 , P ⁡ ( CRL ) ≈ 0.39 P(\text{CRL})\approx 0.39 , P ⁡ ( extension ) ≈ 0.04 P(\text{extension})\approx 0.04 . – Pooling precedents on timing. Each trajectory saw only part of the weekend-PDUFA record. Combining them, with duplicates removed, gives a larger and more consistent sample: * Approvals: 6/6 were dated the preceding weekday and announced that day (Zurzuvae, BYSANTI, YUVIWEL, GENGLYCOS, Opdualag, Daybue). No weekend approval date appears on FDA’s 2023–2025 novel-approval lists. * CRLs: only 2/6 were public by Friday night. * Extension: the closest analogue was announced on the following Monday. * An industry newsletter found by another trajectory says weekend actions “post either Friday after close or Monday pre-market”, which independently supports the risk that a CRL slips past the cutoff. The pooled sample also shows what drives the delay. Both CRLs that FDA issued on a Friday were announced the same afternoon. The late ones were issued on a Saturday, or came from sponsors without US reporting obligations.
From this the team sets outcome-specific chances of being public by the cutoff: about 0.90 0.90 for approval, about 0.45 0.45 for a CRL, about 0.25 0.25 for an extension.
The small chance that FDA does not act at all by Friday is already inside these rates. – Correcting a systematic error. One trajectory assumed a CRL is about as likely as an approval to be public by Friday night. That assumption pushes its crl probability up and its none probability down. The pooled timing evidence contradicts it, so the team corrects the error rather than averaging it in. This is something no single trajectory could have spotted about itself. • Base-rate reasoning. – Decision. The starting point is the 2026 year-to-date approval rate on decision day, about 85%. The team marks this down substantially, because a failed pre-specified primary endpoint in a single 63-patient trial is the typical setting for an efficacy CRL, and Mirum’s own 10-Q names that risk. It then moves part of the way back up for FOP-specific reasons: * the disease is ultra-rare and severe, and about 97% of patients carry the same mutation; * FDA allows one adequate trial plus confirmatory evidence for such conditions; * the volume effect is randomised, durable at 48 weeks, and comes with a clean safety profile. The result is about 0.57 0.57 for approval. – Timing. For a Saturday goal date FDA acts on the preceding weekday, and approvals are announced that same day. A cutoff 1.5 hours before the PDUFA day begins therefore captures almost every approval but only about half of CRLs. – Consequence. none is not neutral uncertainty. It is made up mostly of CRLs and extensions that have not been announced yet. • Prediction. Each decision probability is multiplied by its chance of being public by the cutoff: – approved : 0.57 × 0.90 ≈ 0.51 0.57\times 0.90\approx 0.51 – crl : 0.39 × 0.45 ≈ 0.18 0.39\times 0.45\approx 0.18 – extended : 0.04 × 0.25 ≈ 0.01 0.04\times 0.25\approx 0.01 – none : the remaining 0.30 0.30 Selected option: approved . Rationale: approval is the most likely decision, and the only one almost certain to be visible before the Friday-night cutoff; silence at the cutoff would point to an unannounced CRL. Confidence: moderate. The decision itself is genuinely uncertain, and none of the trajectories could observe the deciding window (ET Sep 24–25). Resolution. FDA approved zilurgisertib, brand name Atebrioz, for FOP. Mirum and Incyte announced it on Friday 2026-09-25: the Business Wire release time-stamped 19:00 ET (23:00 UTC), 3.5 3.5 h before the 22:30 ET cutoff. Mirum’s 8-K filed with the SEC on 2026-09-28 confirms the event date of Sep 25 and the approval.

blocks.en: Question. Mirum Pharmaceuticals’ oral ALK2 inhibitor zilurgisertib (licensed from Incyte) for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is under FDA Priority Review, with a PDUFA target date of Saturday, 2026-09-26. Its pivotal Phase 2 PROGRESS trial missed the primary endpoint (81% reduction in new heterotopic-ossification lesions, p = 0.0986 p=0.0986 ), but reduced new-lesion volume by > 99 % >\!99\% ( p < 0.0001 p<0.0001 ).

Search team trajectory ( τ s \tau_{\mathrm{s}} ). • Decomposition. The scheduler first separates what the question resolves on ( was something announced by the cutoff ) from what it seems to ask ( what FDA decides ). That gives three sub-questions:
(i) premise check: does the drug, the Incyte licence, the Priority Review, and the Saturday PDUFA date really exist as stated;
(ii) timing: given a weekend goal date, how likely is it that FDA acts by Friday, and that the sponsor makes it public before 22:30 ET;
(iii) the decision itself: approval vs. complete response letter (CRL) vs. review extension, weighing a missed primary endpoint against a very strong secondary endpoint and FOP-specific precedent.
It forms an initial forecast ( approved 0.47, crl 0.22, extended 0.03, none 0.28) and then runs three search rounds and one critic call. • Retrieval. Searchers covered: – primary filings: SEC EDGAR full-text search (45 filings mention zilurgisertib), Mirum’s Q1/Q2 2026 10-Q and 8-K filings, and Incyte’s Q2 release, which together confirm the April 2026 licence ($16M upfront, $25M milestone due on approval) and the PDUFA date; – regulator channels: the FDA newsroom and the 2026 Novel Drug Approvals list, both checked up to the last available date; – market and calendar trackers: pdufa.bio decision pages, Mirum’s investor-relations and Business Wire feeds; – trial data: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05090891 and a third-party PDUFA primer, which added the 48-week durability data; – price action: daily MIRM prices compared with the XBI biotech index; – a weekend-PDUFA precedent set: sponsor press-release and 8-K timestamps for 11 cases from 2019–2026 (Zurzuvae, BYSANTI, YUVIWEL, GENGLYCOS, KRESLADI, bitopertin, Joenja, RGX-121, AVT05, deramiocel, tab-cel). • Critique. The critic accepted the evidence base but challenged two calibration choices.
(1) none was being treated as a leftover bucket rather than a modelled outcome. Announcement delay is much more likely after a CRL than after an approval, so P( none ) should sit in the low-to-mid 0.30s, not 0.28.
(2) The earlier FOP drug Sohonos does not license ignoring a failed randomised primary endpoint, so the conditional approval probability should drop from about 0.62 to 0.52–0.58.
It also raised a recency gap: the decisive window (ET Sep 24–25 up to 22:30) had not been observed, so silence through Sep 23 cannot be read as evidence. It requested targeted checks of every public channel up to the cutoff, plus a timing base rate split by outcome. • Evidence summary. – Premise fully verified. As of the last data available (evening ET 2026-09-23), there was no approval, CRL, extension, advisory committee, or major amendment on record. – Mirum’s own 10-Q flags CRL risk. The CEO cited “launch readiness”. The stock fell 11% into the date, including an unexplained − 7 % -7\% day on Sep 18. – Key structural finding: whether an outcome is announced in time depends on what the outcome is. Approvals were public by the Friday before the weekend goal date in 4/4 cases, and FDA has never dated an approval on a weekend. CRLs were public by Friday in only 2/6 cases. The one comparable extension was announced on the following Monday. So none mostly contains CRLs or extensions that had not yet been announced. – Approval case: Sohonos was approved on the same lesion-volume measure from a single-arm study, and recent FDA rare-disease evidence principles support flexibility. CRL case: the pre-specified primary endpoint formally failed in a single trial with only 6 events. – Decision probabilities: approval ≈ 0.58 \approx 0.58 , CRL ≈ 0.35 \approx 0.35 , extension ≈ 0.04 \approx 0.04 . Combined with the outcome-specific announcement probabilities, the forecast is approved 0.52 / crl 0.16 / extended 0.02 / none 0.30. Predict team trajectory ( τ p \tau_{\mathrm{p}} ). • Reconciliation. The predict team receives four independent search trajectories τ 1 , … , τ 4 \tau^{1},\dots,\tau^{4} . It does not average their outputs. It treats them as four partly overlapping evidence sets and re-derives the forecast from the combined evidence. The question resolves on what has been announced by 22:30 ET Friday, so the team splits it into two parts and reconciles each one separately: (i) what FDA actually decides, and (ii) whether that decision is public before the cutoff. – Cross-validated facts. A fact is treated as settled only if at least two trajectories reached it through different sources: * Saturday PDUFA date: Mirum’s 8-K and 10-Q, plus independent PDUFA trackers. * Trial numbers: the missed primary endpoint (1/32 vs. 5/31 patients with new lesions, p = 0.0986 p=0.0986 , only 6 events) against a > 99 % >99\% cut in new-lesion volume. Taken from the company’s filings and from the trial registry or third-party summaries. * No advisory committee and no major amendment. * Nothing announced on any channel up to Sep 23–24: SEC filings, company press releases, the FDA newsroom, and the novel-approval list. One signal comes from a single trajectory only: an unexplained single-day 7% fall in the stock on Sep 18. It is kept, but weighted as weak. – Combining evidence on the decision. Two trajectories reported the Sohonos precedent in two different ways: * one found that FDA accepted “reduction in new heterotopic-ossification volume” as the basis for approving that drug; * another found that this approval rested on a single-arm study compared with natural history. A third trajectory’s critic warned that the precedent may not carry over unless the endpoint and multiplicity design are checked.
Put together, the precedent supports the lesion-volume endpoint (and zilurgisertib’s randomised, placebo-controlled volume result is stronger evidence). It does not settle the failed primary endpoint, which stays a real risk of a complete response letter (CRL). That risk is backed by the 2025–26 efficacy CRLs found in one trajectory.
On the other side, other trajectories added independent cases of rare-disease approval on secondary or surrogate endpoints (tofersen, eteplirsen), plus FDA’s current rare-disease evidence principles.
The trajectories’ own estimates of the approval share span roughly 0.53–0.60. Two of them cited the same third-party approval odds (64–70%). One critic pointed out that these odds refer to eventual approval, not to an approval announced by the cutoff, so the team uses them only as an upper check.
Net result: P ⁡ ( approve ∣ action ) ≈ 0.57 P(\text{approve}\mid\text{action})\approx 0.57 , P ⁡ ( CRL ) ≈ 0.39 P(\text{CRL})\approx 0.39 , P ⁡ ( extension ) ≈ 0.04 P(\text{extension})\approx 0.04 . – Pooling precedents on timing. Each trajectory saw only part of the weekend-PDUFA record. Combining them, with duplicates removed, gives a larger and more consistent sample: * Approvals: 6/6 were dated the preceding weekday and announced that day (Zurzuvae, BYSANTI, YUVIWEL, GENGLYCOS, Opdualag, Daybue). No weekend approval date appears on FDA’s 2023–2025 novel-approval lists. * CRLs: only 2/6 were public by Friday night. * Extension: the closest analogue was announced on the following Monday. * An industry newsletter found by another trajectory says weekend actions “post either Friday after close or Monday pre-market”, which independently supports the risk that a CRL slips past the cutoff. The pooled sample also shows what drives the delay. Both CRLs that FDA issued on a Friday were announced the same afternoon. The late ones were issued on a Saturday, or came from sponsors without US reporting obligations.
From this the team sets outcome-specific chances of being public by the cutoff: about 0.90 0.90 for approval, about 0.45 0.45 for a CRL, about 0.25 0.25 for an extension.
The small chance that FDA does not act at all by Friday is already inside these rates. – Correcting a systematic error. One trajectory assumed a CRL is about as likely as an approval to be public by Friday night. That assumption pushes its crl probability up and its none probability down. The pooled timing evidence contradicts it, so the team corrects the error rather than averaging it in. This is something no single trajectory could have spotted about itself. • Base-rate reasoning. – Decision. The starting point is the 2026 year-to-date approval rate on decision day, about 85%. The team marks this down substantially, because a failed pre-specified primary endpoint in a single 63-patient trial is the typical setting for an efficacy CRL, and Mirum’s own 10-Q names that risk. It then moves part of the way back up for FOP-specific reasons: * the disease is ultra-rare and severe, and about 97% of patients carry the same mutation; * FDA allows one adequate trial plus confirmatory evidence for such conditions; * the volume effect is randomised, durable at 48 weeks, and comes with a clean safety profile. The result is about 0.57 0.57 for approval. – Timing. For a Saturday goal date FDA acts on the preceding weekday, and approvals are announced that same day. A cutoff 1.5 hours before the PDUFA day begins therefore captures almost every approval but only about half of CRLs. – Consequence. none is not neutral uncertainty. It is made up mostly of CRLs and extensions that have not been announced yet. • Prediction. Each decision probability is multiplied by its chance of being public by the cutoff: – approved : 0.57 × 0.90 ≈ 0.51 0.57\times 0.90\approx 0.51 – crl : 0.39 × 0.45 ≈ 0.18 0.39\times 0.45\approx 0.18 – extended : 0.04 × 0.25 ≈ 0.01 0.04\times 0.25\approx 0.01 – none : the remaining 0.30 0.30 Selected option: approved . Rationale: approval is the most likely decision, and the only one almost certain to be visible before the Friday-night cutoff; silence at the cutoff would point to an unannounced CRL. Confidence: moderate. The decision itself is genuinely uncertain, and none of the trajectories could observe the deciding window (ET Sep 24–25). Resolution. FDA approved zilurgisertib, brand name Atebrioz, for FOP. Mirum and Incyte announced it on Friday 2026-09-25: the Business Wire release time-stamped 19:00 ET (23:00 UTC), 3.5 3.5 h before the 22:30 ET cutoff. Mirum’s 8-K filed with the SEC on 2026-09-28 confirms the event date of Sep 25 and the approval.

blocks.en:
Critique. The critic accepted the evidence base but challenged two calibration choices.
(1) none was being treated as a leftover bucket rather than a modelled outcome. Announcement delay is much more likely after a CRL than after an approval, so P( none ) should sit in the low-to-mid 0.30s, not 0.28.
(2) The earlier FOP drug Sohonos does not license ignoring a failed randomised primary endpoint, so the conditional approval probability should drop from about 0.62 to 0.52–0.58.
It also raised a recency gap: the decisive window (ET Sep 24–25 up to 22:30) had not been observed, so silence through Sep 23 cannot be read as evidence. It requested targeted checks of every public channel up to the cutoff, plus a timing base rate split by outcome.

(2)更早的FOP药物Sohonos不许可忽略一个失败的随机化主终点,因此有条件的批准概率应该从0.62左右下降到0.52–0.58.
也引起了一个复议空白:决定性的窗口(ET Sep 24–25至22:30)没有被遵守,因此通过Sep 23的沉默不能被看成是证据. 它要求有针对性地检查每个公共渠道直至停工为止,并按结果划分计时基准率。

blocks.en: Evidence summary. – Premise fully verified. As of the last data available (evening ET 2026-09-23), there was no approval, CRL, extension, advisory committee, or major amendment on record. – Mirum’s own 10-Q flags CRL risk. blocks.en:
Reconciliation. The predict team receives four independent search trajectories τ 1 , … , τ 4 \tau^{1},\dots,\tau^{4} . It does not average their outputs. It treats them as four partly overlapping evidence sets and re-derives the forecast from the combined evidence. The question resolves on what has been announced by 22:30 ET Friday, so the team splits it into two parts and reconciles each one separately: (i) what FDA actually decides, and (ii) whether that decision is public before the cutoff. – Cross-validated facts. A fact is treated as settled only if at least two trajectories reached it through different sources: * Saturday PDUFA date: Mirum’s 8-K and 10-Q, plus independent PDUFA trackers. * Trial numbers: the missed primary endpoint (1/32 vs. 5/31 patients with new lesions, p = 0.0986 p=0.0986 , only 6 events) against a > 99 % >99\% cut in new-lesion volume. Taken from the company’s filings and from the trial registry or third-party summaries. * No advisory committee and no major amendment. * Nothing announced on any channel up to Sep 23–24: SEC filings, company press releases, the FDA newsroom, and the novel-approval list. One signal comes from a single trajectory only: an unexplained single-day 7% fall in the stock on Sep 18. It is kept, but weighted as weak. – Combining evidence on the decision. Two trajectories reported the Sohonos precedent in two different ways: * one found that FDA accepted “reduction in new heterotopic-ossification volume” as the basis for approving that drug; * another found that this approval rested on a single-arm study compared with natural history. A third trajectory’s critic warned that the precedent may not carry over unless the endpoint and multiplicity design are checked.
Put together, the precedent supports the lesion-volume endpoint (and zilurgisertib’s randomised, placebo-controlled volume result is stronger evidence). It does not settle the failed primary endpoint, which stays a real risk of a complete response letter (CRL). That risk is backed by the 2025–26 efficacy CRLs found in one trajectory.
On the other side, other trajectories added independent cases of rare-disease approval on secondary or surrogate endpoints (tofersen, eteplirsen), plus FDA’s current rare-disease evidence principles.
The trajectories’ own estimates of the approval share span roughly 0.53–0.60. Two of them cited the same third-party approval odds (64–70%). One critic pointed out that these odds refer to eventual approval, not to an approval announced by the cutoff, so the team uses them only as an upper check.
Net result: P ⁡ ( approve ∣ action ) ≈ 0.57 P(\text{approve}\mid\text{action})\approx 0.57 , P ⁡ ( CRL ) ≈ 0.39 P(\text{CRL})\approx 0.39 , P ⁡ ( extension ) ≈ 0.04 P(\text{extension})\approx 0.04 . – Pooling precedents on timing. Each trajectory saw only part of the weekend-PDUFA record. Combining them, with duplicates removed, gives a larger and more consistent sample: * Approvals: 6/6 were dated the preceding weekday and announced that day (Zurzuvae, BYSANTI, YUVIWEL, GENGLYCOS, Opdualag, Daybue). No weekend approval date appears on FDA’s 2023–2025 novel-approval lists. * CRLs: only 2/6 were public by Friday night. * Extension: the closest analogue was announced on the following Monday. * An industry newsletter found by another trajectory says weekend actions “post either Friday after close or Monday pre-market”, which independently supports the risk that a CRL slips past the cutoff. The pooled sample also shows what drives the delay. Both CRLs that FDA issued on a Friday were announced the same afternoon. The late ones were issued on a Saturday, or came from sponsors without US reporting obligations.
From this the team sets outcome-specific chances of being public by the cutoff: about 0.90 0.90 for approval, about 0.45 0.45 for a CRL, about 0.25 0.25 for an extension.
The small chance that FDA does not act at all by Friday is already inside these rates. – Correcting a systematic error. One trajectory assumed a CRL is about as likely as an approval to be public by Friday night. That assumption pushes its crl probability up and its none probability down. The pooled timing evidence contradicts it, so the team corrects the error rather than averaging it in. This is something no single trajectory could have spotted about itself.

blocks.en: Base-rate reasoning. – Decision. The starting point is the 2026 year-to-date approval rate on decision day, about 85%. The team marks this down substantially, because a failed pre-specified primary endpoint in a single 63-patient trial is the typical setting for an efficacy CRL, and Mirum’s own 10-Q names that risk. It then moves part of the way back up for FOP-specific reasons: * the disease is ultra-rare and severe, and about 97% of patients carry the same mutation; * FDA allows one adequate trial plus confirmatory evidence for such conditions; * the volume effect is randomised, durable at 48 weeks, and comes with a clean safety profile. The result is about 0.57 0.57 for approval. – Timing. For a Saturday goal date FDA acts on the preceding weekday, and approvals are announced that same day. A cutoff 1.5 hours before the PDUFA day begins therefore captures almost every approval but only about half of CRLs. – Consequence. none is not neutral uncertainty. It is made up mostly of CRLs and extensions that have not been announced yet.
blocks.zh: 基础率推理 – 决定. 起点是决定日的2026年至今批准率,约为85%. 团队将这一点大幅降低,因为在63名患者的单一试验中,一个预先指定的初级终点失败,是疗效CRL的典型设定,而Mirum自己的10Q名也冒了风险. 之后,由于FOP的具体原因,它会移动部分退路: *该疾病是超稀有和严重的,大约97%的患者携带同样的突变; *FDA允许对此类情况进行一次充分的试验并附加确认证据; *体积效应是随机的,持续了48周,并带有干净的安全简介. 结果大约为0.57 0.57批准。 - 时机 对于星期六的目标日期,林业发展局在上个工作日采取行动,并于同日宣布批准。 因此,在PDUFA日开始前1.5小时的截止日期几乎获得所有批准,但只有大约一半的CRL。 – 说吧 – 相会相会. 没有一个不是中立的不确定性。 它主要由尚未宣布的CRL和扩展组成.

blocks.en: Prediction. Each decision probability is multiplied by its chance of being public by the cutoff: – approved : 0.57 × 0.90 ≈ 0.51 0.57\times 0.90\approx 0.51 – crl : 0.39 × 0.45 ≈ 0.18 0.39\times 0.45\approx 0.18 – extended : 0.04 × 0.25 ≈ 0.01 0.04\times 0.25\approx 0.01 – none : the remaining 0.30 0.30 Selected option: approved . Rationale: approval is the most likely decision, and the only one almost certain to be visible before the Friday-night cutoff; silence at the cutoff would point to an unannounced CRL. Confidence: moderate. The decision itself is genuinely uncertain, and none of the trajectories could observe the deciding window (ET Sep 24–25).
